`system/pacman.sh` holds the parts of `system/deploy`'s package convergence that
model someone else's rules: the list format plus the per-host overlay, and the
single `Include` line appended to `/etc/pacman.conf` (whole-line matched, so the
stock config's commented-out examples don't read as "already enabled"). The
cases source it and run against a temp tree through its `SUDO` seam, then hand a
copy of this host's real `pacman.conf` to `pacman-conf` to confirm pacman does
glob an `Include` and does register a `[multilib]` section reached through one --
the assumption the whole drop-in design rests on. Nothing writes to `/etc`, and
no case needs root.

`system/thermald-setup` (run from `system/deploy`) is the *enable* half that a
package list cannot express: `pacman -S` installs a unit, it does not start one.
Which hosts want thermald is decided upstream of it, by `thermald` appearing in
`system/packages.<host>` — so the script's own gate is just "is it installed",
and a host whose list never asked for it is one it never touches. The cases drive
the real script with stub `pacman`/`sudo`/`systemctl` on `PATH`, asserting both
halves: a host without the package does nothing at all, and a converged host
escalates zero times.

The `_ghostty_saved_ps1` priming in `zsh.nix` is a model of ghostty's
`ghostty-integration`: it pre-sets variables private to that script so its own
`ps1_changed` guard fires on the first precmd, which is what stops the PS1
rewrite that corrupts powerlevel10k's `PROMPT` into a literal `}}`. Rename those
variables upstream and nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
symptom is the artifact coming back. The cases render the *live generated* config
in a pty -- both the injected and plain startup paths -- and assert the `}}` is
gone with the line and still returns without it, so a workaround that has quietly
stopped working fails out loud, and so does one that has become unnecessary.

`STEAM_FORCE_DESKTOPUI_SCALING` (in `home.nix`) models Steam's side of a bargain
Hyprland can't enforce: `xwayland.force_zero_scaling` hands X11 clients real
pixels and no DPI hint, and Steam's CEF UI reads neither `Xft.dpi` nor
`GDK_DPI_SCALE`, so on a scaled panel it draws tiny until told its own factor.
The cases evaluate three hosts and derive every expectation from the config
itself — the var must equal the scale that host's eDP-1 monitor rule asks for,
and be unset where there is no such rule — so the pair can't drift apart
silently, which is the only way this fails. A fourth case asserts a scaled host
still exists, since otherwise all three would pass vacuously.

p='home.nix'; s=open(p).read()
# Stage 1 state: permit gone + test referenced; sandbox still present (its own commit).
old = """  # No permittedInsecurePackages entry: nothing here needs one, which
  # tests/insecure-packages.sh holds to rather than a comment that a lock bump
  # can quietly falsify. (`sandbox` used to be set here too, doing nothing --
  # it is a nix.conf setting, not a nixpkgs config attr, and nixpkgs' freeform
  # config type swallows undeclared attrs without so much as a warning unless
  # warnUndeclaredOptions is on. The real knob lives in nix.settings, and CI
  # deliberately runs with sandbox = false; see docs/ci-nix-home.md.)
  nixpkgs.config.allowUnfree = true;
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s = s.replace(old, """  # No permittedInsecurePackages entry: nothing here needs one, and
  # tests/insecure-packages.sh holds that rather than a comment a lock bump can
  # quietly falsify -- which is exactly how the entry this replaces went stale.
  nixpkgs.config = {
    allowUnfree = true;
    sandbox = true;
  };
""")
# Point the vesktop comment at the test instead of asking a human to remember.
old2 = """    # not flag, so it needs no permittedInsecurePackages entry -- verify that
    # still holds after a lock bump rather than trusting this comment.
"""
assert s.count(old2)==1
s = s.replace(old2, """    # not flag, so it needs no permittedInsecurePackages entry --
    # tests/insecure-packages.sh is what keeps that true across a lock bump.
""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git add -A && git -c user.name="Sauyon Lee" commit -q --amend -F - <<'EOF'
nixpkgs: drop the electron-39.8.10 permit, and test that nothing needs one

The entry was scoped to an exact version precisely so that a
bitwarden-desktop bump onto a different Electron would re-raise the flag
for review. The bump happened and nobody noticed: the comment still said
bitwarden-desktop 2026.6.1 pins electron 39.8.10, while the lock has
2026.9.0 on electron 43.6.0. So the permit had quietly become a no-op,
and a stale exception is worse than none -- it reads as though something
still depends on an EOL Electron.

Replacing it with another scoped comment would fail the same way, so the
claim gets a test. nixpkgs raises its insecure-package error while
*evaluating* the flagged derivation, and forcing activationPackage.drvPath
instantiates every input derivation transitively -- so with no permit in
the config, "every host evaluates" is the whole claim rather than a proxy
for it. tests/insecure-packages.sh drives that over every host listed in
the flake (read from the flake, not written down, since a permit is global
config and a hand-maintained list would silently stop covering a new host).

Its last case is the teeth: every host case above passes vacuously if
nixpkgs stops flagging things, or if some later config turns the check off
wholesale, so a package nixpkgs still flags must throw under this repo's
own nixpkgs. Watched fail before being trusted -- planting pkgs.electron_39
in the desktop block fails the three desktop Linux hosts by name and
leaves the other three green, which is also the granularity working.

Verified: all six hosts (shiori, fujiwara, kyuusaku, setsuna, utsuho,
mari) evaluate with the attribute deleted, and the closure contains
electron-43.6.0 and no electron-39 at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

nixpkgs: drop sandbox = true, which was never a nixpkgs config attr

`sandbox` is a nix.conf setting. It is not declared anywhere in nixpkgs'
pkgs/top-level/config.nix, so it landed in that module's freeform
`lazyAttrsOf raw` type, which accepts undeclared attrs silently -- the only
surfacing is a warning gated on config.warnUndeclaredOptions, and that
defaults to false. So the line has been inert for as long as it has been
there, asking for sandboxing somewhere sandboxing is not configured.

"Three desktop Linux hosts fail, other three green" is right — the block is `lib.optionals (!isDarwin && isDesktop)`, so shiori/setsuna/utsuho, leaving fujiwara/kyuusaku/mari.

content.content:
# Weekly CVE scan of the utsuho home closure with vulnix. The job log is the
# report. See docs/ci-vulnix-scan.md.
#
# Never fails on findings: vulnix exits non-zero on any CVE match and this
# closure always matches some (false positives, build-only bootstraps,
# unpatched-upstream), so a red pipeline would be noise. Green = the scan ran.
name: vulnix-scan

on:
  schedule:
    # Mondays 06:00 UTC. Standard 5-field cron, not Woodpecker's 6-field form.
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  scan:
    # See nix-home.yml — privilege comes from the runner. This job normally
    # only substitutes, but must be able to build when attic is cold.
    runs-on: privileged
    container:
      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
    env:
      NIX_CONFIG: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
        # In-cluster Service, not https://attic.ko.ag/kube — see nix-home.yml for
        # why: the Cloudflare hairpin caps a single response at 600s, and the
        # 2.44 GiB google-fonts NAR cannot land inside it.
        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
=== rest ===
    steps:
      # Needed even though this job only reads: attic is not anonymously
      # readable and nix ignores a substituter it cannot authenticate to, so
      # without this the scan rebuilds the closure instead of fetching it.
      - name: authorise nix against attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
          umask 077
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

      # Hand-rolled: actions/checkout cannot run in this image (no node).
      - name: checkout
        run: |
          set -eu
          git clone https://forge.ko.ag/${{ github.repository }}.git .
          git checkout --detach ${{ github.sha }}
          git --no-pager log -1 --oneline

      - name: realise utsuho closure
        run: |
          set -eu
          # --fallback: build a path locally rather than abort the scan when a
          # substituter dies mid-NAR.
          nix build --fallback --no-link --print-out-paths \
            .#homeConfigurations.utsuho.activationPackage > /tmp/drv
          cat /tmp/drv

      # `|| true` keeps the step green on findings — see the header.
      - name: scan
        run: |
          set -eu
          export DRV=$(cat /tmp/drv)
          nix shell \
            github:NixOS/nixpkgs/29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299#vulnix \
            github:NixOS/nixpkgs/29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299#jq \
            -c sh -c '
              vulnix --json "$DRV" > vulnix.json || true
              count=$(jq "length" vulnix.json)
              echo "======================================================"
              echo "  vulnix: $count affected packages in utsuho closure"
              echo "======================================================"
              echo "affected-CVEs  package  (top 60 by CVE count)"
              jq -r ".[] | \"\(.affected_by | length)\t\(.name)\"" vulnix.json \
                | sort -rn | head -60
            '

input.command:
cat > tests/insecure-packages.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the claim that nothing in this config needs a permittedInsecurePackages
# entry -- the claim home.nix's nixpkgs.config block now makes by having no such
# entry at all.
#
# Why this needs a test rather than a comment. The entry that used to live there
# was scoped to "electron-39.8.10" precisely so that a bitwarden-desktop bump onto
# a different Electron would re-raise the flag for review. The bump happened and
# nobody noticed: the comment still described bitwarden-desktop 2026.6.1 on
# electron 39.8.10 long after the lock had moved to 2026.9.0 on electron 43.6.0,
# so the permit sat there as a dangling exception that read like a live dependency
# on an EOL Electron. A scoped comment is exactly the thing that goes stale
# silently across a lock bump; this file is the same intent expressed as something
# that fails.
#
# Not the same job as .forgejo/workflows/vulnix-scan.yml. That scans the realised
# closure for CVEs weekly and never fails, because this closure always matches
# some. This asks a narrower question with a yes/no answer: does anything here
# need nixpkgs' *insecure* flag switched off. One is a report, this is a gate.
#
# What is actually being protected here, in three parts:
#
#   No host needs a permit. nixpkgs raises its insecure-package error while
#   *evaluating* the flagged derivation, and forcing activationPackage.drvPath
#   instantiates every input derivation transitively -- so with no permit in the
#   config, "every host evaluates" is the claim itself, not a proxy for it. The
#   host list is read out of the flake rather than written down, because this is
#   global config: a new host added to flake.nix is covered the day it lands, and
#   a hand-maintained case list would silently stop covering it.
#
#   The check is still live, under each host's own config. "Every host evaluates"

old = """  # `sandbox` used to be set here too, doing nothing: it is a nix.conf setting,
  # not a nixpkgs config attr, and nixpkgs' freeform config type swallows
  # undeclared attrs without even a warning unless warnUndeclaredOptions is on.
  # Everywhere that actually wants a value sets it where nix reads it: these boxes
  # via system/etc/nix/nix.custom.conf, and CI via NIX_CONFIG in its workflows,
  # which force it back on because the runner image ships sandbox = false.
  nixpkgs.config.allowUnfree = true;
"""
assert final.count(old)==1
inter = final.replace(old, """  nixpkgs.config = {
    allowUnfree = true;
    sandbox = true;

git add -A && git -c user.name="Sauyon Lee" commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
nixpkgs: drop the electron-39.8.10 permit, and test that nothing needs one

The entry was scoped to an exact version precisely so that a
bitwarden-desktop bump onto a different Electron would re-raise the flag
for review. The bump happened and nobody noticed: the comment still said
bitwarden-desktop 2026.6.1 pins electron 39.8.10, while the lock has
2026.9.0 on electron 43.6.0. So the permit had quietly become a no-op,
and a stale exception is worse than none -- it reads as though something
still depends on an EOL Electron.

Replacing it with another scoped comment would fail the same way, so the
claim gets a test. nixpkgs raises its insecure-package error while
*evaluating* the flagged derivation, and forcing activationPackage.drvPath
instantiates every input derivation transitively -- so with no permit in
the config, "every host evaluates" is the claim rather than a proxy for
it. tests/insecure-packages.sh drives that over every host in the flake,
plus mari's darwin system, which carries its own nixpkgs.config that
home.nix has no authority over. Both lists are read from the flake, not
written down, since a hand-maintained one silently stops covering a host
added later.

The teeth are a second case per host, and they are the part worth
explaining. "Every host evaluates" is also true of a config that has
turned the check off, and it turns off in more ways than one: besides the
permit list there is allowInsecurePredicate, which check-meta.nix
short-circuits on *before* it consults that list, so one line makes every
insecure package everywhere evaluate. A canary evaluated under a config
this test made up could not see either. So it goes through
homeConfigurations.<host>.pkgs -- the host's real nixpkgs with the real
config attached -- and has to fail with nixpkgs' "marked as insecure"
specifically, because a canary that merely failed to evaluate would pass
on a typo, a renamed attr or a fetch error, which is the one case whose
whole job is to not pass for the wrong reason.

Watched fail on each regression before being trusted, all three of which
the earlier draft of this test reported green:
  - allowInsecurePredicate = _: true            -> 6 of 13 fail
  - the scoped permit re-added, with electron_39 -> 6 of 13 fail
  - canary pointed at a nonexistent attr        -> fails "for the wrong reason"

Verified: all six hosts and the darwin system evaluate with the attribute
deleted, and shiori's closure holds electron-43.6.0 and no electron-39.

Not the same job as .forgejo/workflows/vulnix-scan.yml, which scans the
realised closure for CVEs weekly and never fails because this closure
always matches some. That is a report; this is a gate.

`sandbox` is a nix.conf setting. It is not declared anywhere in nixpkgs'
pkgs/top-level/config.nix, so it landed in that module's freeform
`lazyAttrsOf raw` type, which accepts undeclared attrs silently -- the only
surfacing is a warning gated on config.warnUndeclaredOptions, and that
defaults to false. So the line has been inert for as long as it has been

activationPackage.drvPath is byte-identical either way.

Everywhere that actually wants a value sets it where nix reads it. These
boxes get it from system/etc/nix/nix.custom.conf, and both CI workflows set
`sandbox = true` in NIX_CONFIG because the runner image ships it off and
unsandboxed builds fail there. Nothing wanted a different value from
home-manager; the line just looked like it did.

# nit: duplicated phrase, an editing artifact.

#   would pass on a typo, a renamed attr, an unsupported platform or a fetch
#   error -- the one case whose whole job is to stop this file passing for the
#   wrong reason, passing for the wrong reason. So its stderr has to actually say
#   the package was refused as insecure.

s = s.replace(old, """#   It throws for the *right* reason. A canary that merely "failed to evaluate"
#   would pass on a typo, a renamed attr, an unsupported platform or a fetch
#   error -- which would leave the one case whose whole job is to catch a vacuous
#   pass being a vacuous pass itself. So its stderr has to actually say the
#   package was refused as insecure.
""")

# nit: exit 1 inside a process substitution only kills the subshell, and the
# caller then prints the misleading "no homeConfigurations" line anyway.
old2 = """attrs_of() { # attrs_of <output>
  if ! nix eval --json "$FLAKE#$1" --apply builtins.attrNames >"$D/out" 2>"$D/err"; then
    echo >&2; echo "could not list $1:" >&2; cat "$D/err" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  jq -r '.[]' <"$D/out"
}

mapfile -t hosts < <(attrs_of homeConfigurations)
[ "${#hosts[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "flake defines no homeConfigurations" >&2; exit 1; }
"""
assert s.count(old2)==1
s = s.replace(old2, """# Fills the global `names` with one attr per line. Not a pipeline and not a
# process substitution: piping into jq hands the pipeline jq's status, and jq
# exits 0 on empty stdin, which would turn a broken checkout into an empty list
# reported as "this flake has no hosts" -- and an `exit` inside a `< <(...)`
# would kill only the subshell, letting that same wrong message print anyway.
names=()
attrs_of() { # attrs_of <output> [optional]
  names=()
  if ! nix eval --json "$FLAKE#$1" --apply builtins.attrNames >"$D/out" 2>"$D/err"; then
    # An output this flake simply does not define is only an error when the
    # caller says the output is required. Anything else is a broken checkout and
    # is fatal either way -- never a silently empty list, which would drop every
    # case below it and still exit green.
    if [ "${2-}" = optional ] && grep -q 'does not provide attribute' "$D/err"; then
      return 0
    fi
    echo >&2; echo "could not list $1:" >&2; cat "$D/err" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  mapfile -t names < <(jq -r '.[]' <"$D/out")
}

attrs_of homeConfigurations
hosts=("${names[@]}")
[ "${#hosts[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "flake defines no homeConfigurations" >&2; exit 1; }
"""	)

# nit: the darwin listing swallowed every error, so a coverage loss read as green.
old3 = """mapfile -t systems < <(nix eval --json "$FLAKE#darwinConfigurations" \\
                         --apply builtins.attrNames 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[]' || true)
for sys in ${systems+"${systems[@]}"}; do
  if nix eval --raw "$FLAKE#darwinConfigurations.$sys.system.drvPath" \\
       >/dev/null 2>"$D/err"; then
    pass "darwin system $sys evaluates with no permittedInsecurePackages entry"
  else
    fail "darwin system $sys needs a permittedInsecurePackages entry" \\
         "$(grep -iE 'marked as insecure|error:' "$D/err" | head -2 | tr '\\n' ' ')"
  fi
done
"""
assert s.count(old3)==1
s = s.replace(old3, """attrs_of darwinConfigurations optional
for sys in ${names+"${names[@]}"}; do
  if nix eval --raw "$FLAKE#darwinConfigurations.$sys.system.drvPath" \\
       >/dev/null 2>"$D/err"; then
    pass "darwin system $sys evaluates with no permittedInsecurePackages entry"
  else
    fail "darwin system $sys needs a permittedInsecurePackages entry" \\
         "$(grep -iE 'marked as insecure|error:' "$D/err" | head -2 | tr '\\n' ' ')"
    echo "     full eval output:"; sed 's/^/     /' "$D/err"
  fi
done
"""	)
open(p,'w').write(s)

nixpkgs: drop the electron-39.8.10 permit, and test that nothing needs one

The entry was scoped to an exact version precisely so that a
bitwarden-desktop bump onto a different Electron would re-raise the flag
for review. The bump happened and nobody noticed: the comment still said
bitwarden-desktop 2026.6.1 pins electron 39.8.10, while the lock has
2026.9.0 on electron 43.6.0. So the permit had quietly become a no-op,
and a stale exception is worse than none -- it reads as though something
still depends on an EOL Electron.

Replacing it with another scoped comment would fail the same way, so the
claim gets a test. nixpkgs raises its insecure-package error while
*evaluating* the flagged derivation, and forcing activationPackage.drvPath
instantiates every input derivation transitively -- so with no permit in
the config, "every host evaluates" is the claim rather than a proxy for
it. tests/insecure-packages.sh drives that over every host in the flake,
plus mari's darwin system, which carries its own nixpkgs.config that
home.nix has no authority over. Both lists are read from the flake, not
written down, since a hand-maintained one silently stops covering a host
added later.

The teeth are a second case per host, and they are the part worth
explaining. "Every host evaluates" is also true of a config that has
turned the check off, and it turns off in more ways than one: besides the
permit list there is allowInsecurePredicate, which check-meta.nix
short-circuits on *before* it consults that list, so one line makes every
insecure package everywhere evaluate. A canary evaluated under a config
this test made up could not see either. So it goes through
homeConfigurations.<host>.pkgs -- the host's real nixpkgs with the real
config attached -- and has to fail with nixpkgs' "marked as insecure"
specifically, because a canary that merely failed to evaluate would pass
on a typo, a renamed attr or a fetch error, which would leave the one case
whose job is to catch a vacuous pass being a vacuous pass itself.

Watched fail on each regression before being trusted, all three of which
an earlier draft of this test reported green:
  - allowInsecurePredicate = _: true             -> 6 of 13 fail
  - the scoped permit re-added, with electron_39 -> 6 of 13 fail
  - canary pointed at a nonexistent attr         -> fails "for the wrong reason"

A listing that fails is fatal rather than an empty list, since an empty
one drops every case under it and still exits green; an output the flake
does not define at all is the one tolerated case, and only where the
caller marks it optional. Both paths exercised: a required output missing
exits 1 with nix's own error, an optional one runs the remaining 12.

deleted, and shiori's closure holds electron-43.6.0 and no electron-39.

Not the same job as .forgejo/workflows/vulnix-scan.yml, which scans the
realised closure for CVEs weekly and never fails because this closure
always matches some. That is a report; this is a gate.

compiled-in default, which is on. The one place it is set deliberately is
CI: both workflows put `sandbox = true` in NIX_CONFIG because the runner
image ships it off and unsandboxed builds fail there. Nothing wanted a
different value from home-manager; the line just looked like it did.

Both nits fixed. Branch `add-vesktop` is 3 commits on `ab63d24`, still **not merged**.

**1. Dead `sandbox = true` removed.** Confirmed inert: not declared in nixpkgs' `config.nix`, absorbed by its freeform type, warning off by default. Removal is byte-identical — `utsuho`'s drvPath unchanged.

**2. `tests/insecure-packages.sh` added — 13 cases, all passing.** Review found my first draft was **green on the exact regression it existed to prevent**. Rewrote it: the canary now runs through `homeConfigurations.<host>.pkgs`, the host's real nixpkgs with the real config. Watched it fail on all three:
- `allowInsecurePredicate = _: true` → 6 of 13 fail (old draft: passed 7/7)
- scoped permit re-added + `electron_39` → 6 of 13 fail (old draft: passed 7/7)
- canary pointed at a bad attr → fails *"for the wrong reason"*, not a pass

**3. Two false claims of mine, both caught and fixed.** I wrote that CI "deliberately runs with sandbox = false" — CI sets `sandbox = true` because the *image* ships it off. Then my fix claimed the boxes get it from `nix.custom.conf`; that file sets no `sandbox` and nothing in the repo does — they use nix's default. Both corrected in `home.nix` and the commit message.

**4. Full suite:** `insecure-packages` 13/13, plus 7 other suites green. `ghostty-p10k-prompt` (1/13) and `wif-tpm` (1/10) fail — **pre-existing**, identical on master.

**5. Review record, honestly:** the drovr panel's `correctness` angle died repeatedly (degenerate backend output), so it never hit two consecutive clean rounds. It delivered all four angles clean once on this exact HEAD; I covered correctness with three independent read-only reviewers, which is where every real finding came from. No Critical or Important remains open.
